nodes.step: unlisted: implement sleep_cycle.mint() and close() in cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/sleep_cycle.py
nodes.assumption: mint() is called by the idle-detection trigger (child 9b6b392ebcfe) when idle is detected, creates a TOKEN, posts it to announce, and returns it for the caller to track cycle completion. close() is called when the token returns to cairn and completes the cycle. Forward logic is in per-device probes (child bf146e9e3967), not here.
nodes.would_settle: Specify: Does mint() call announce.post() itself or return a message for the ground loop to post? What is the signature of the trigger callback? Where in ground_loop is mint() invoked?

nodes.step: unlisted: implement token circulation: route token through device roster in alpha order from ground_loop discovery.py using announce channel and per-device probes
nodes.assumption: Each device's sleep probe (built by child bf146e9e3967) matches the incoming token, optionally runs sleep work, and forwards the token to the next device in alpha order (discovery.py roster). The circulation is entirely message-driven on the announce channel; no polling, no central loop.
nodes.would_settle: Specify: Is forwarding logic centralized in sleep_cycle.py (a loop posting to each device in sequence) or distributed (each device's probe forwards)? How does a device determine the next device's address from the roster?
